facts.statement: Fossils of Caudipteryx were recovered in 1997 from the Sihetun locality in Liaoning province, China.
facts.quote: In 1997, several well-preserved dinosaur skeletons were recovered from the Jiulongsong Member of the Chaomidianzi Formation (now Jianshangou Bed of the Yixian Formation), at the Sihetun locality of Liaoning province, China.

facts.statement: The name Caudipteryx means "tail feather" and the species name zoui honors Zou Jiahua, a former vice premier of China.
facts.quote: The generic name, Caudipteryx, means "tail feather", and the specific name, zoui, is in honor of Zou Jiahua for his prominent support to the scientific community as the vice premier of China.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton of Caudipteryx was found in 1988 at the Zhangjiagou locality, 3 km from the main discovery site.
facts.quote: Around the summer of 1988, a partially complete skeleton of Caudipteryx lacking the skull was found in sediments of the "Layer 6" of the Yixian Formation, at the Zhangjiagou locality, which is set apart 3 km from Sihetun.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx lived in China during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 124.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx (meaning "tail feather") is a genus of small oviraptorosaurian dinosaurs that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous, around 124.6 million years ago.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx was a small, feathered dinosaur with an appearance so bird-like that some scientists initially thought it was a bird.
facts.quote: They were feathered and extremely bird-like in their overall appearance, to the point that some paleontologists suggested it was a bird.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx was a small theropod measuring between 72.5 and 89 cm in length and weighing about 5 kg.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx was a small theropod, measuring 72.5 - 89 cm long and weighing about 5 kg based on femur length.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx had symmetrical, vane-bearing feathers on its hands that measured between 15 and 20 cm in length.
facts.quote: The hands of Caudipteryx supported symmetrical, pennaceous feathers that had vanes and barbs, measuring between 15 and 20 cm long.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx possessed a fan of feathers on its tail.
facts.quote: An additional fan of feathers existed on its tail.

facts.statement: The body of C. zoui was covered in black feathers, with a preserved banding pattern on the tail feathers.
facts.quote: The body of C. zoui was covered in black feathers, with a visible banding pattern preserved on tail feathers.

facts.statement: Studies of its flight feather count suggest that Caudipteryx was secondarily flightless.
facts.quote: A study on the number of flight feathers has concluded that Caudipteryx was secondarily flightless.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx is thought to have been an omnivore, as gastroliths are preserved in at least two specimens.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx is thought to have been an omnivore. In at least two specimens of Caudipteryx (NGMC 97 4 A and NGMC 97 9 A), gastroliths are preserved.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Caudipteryx come from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: All Caudipteryx fossils were recovered from the Yixian Formation in Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The consensus classification places Caudipteryx as a basal member of the Oviraptorosauria, a group of non-avian theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The consensus view, based on several cladistic analyses, is that Caudipteryx is a basal (primitive) member of the Oviraptorosauria, and the oviraptorosaurians are non-avian theropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that Caudipteryx belongs within the bird lineage (Aves) rather than being a non-avian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Halszka Osmólska et al. (2004) ran a cladistic analysis that came to a different conclusion. They found that the most birdlike features of oviraptorids actually place the whole clade within Aves itself, meaning that Caudipteryx is both an oviraptorid and a bird.

facts.statement: A minority of researchers believe Caudipteryx is a flightless bird that evolved from non-dinosaurian archosaurs, not a theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Others, such as Stephen Czerkas and Larry Martin have concluded that Caudipteryx is not a theropod dinosaur at all. They believe that Caudipteryx, like all maniraptorans, is a flightless bird, and that birds evolved from non-dinosaurian archosaurs.

facts.statement: Paleornithologist Alan Feduccia argues that Caudipteryx is a flightless bird that evolved from earlier archosaurs, not from theropods.
facts.quote: Paleornithologist Alan Feduccia sees Caudipteryx as a flightless bird evolving from earlier archosaurian dinosaurs rather than from late theropods.

facts.statement: Jones et al. (2000) used mathematical comparisons of body proportions to conclude that Caudipteryx was a bird.
facts.quote: Jones et al. (2000) found that Caudipteryx was a bird based on a mathematical comparison of the body proportions of flightless birds and non-avian theropods.

facts.statement: Dyke and Norell (2005) criticized the mathematical methods used to classify Caudipteryx as a bird and concluded it was a non-avian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Dyke and Norell (2005) criticized this result for flaws in their mathematical methods, and produced results of their own which supported the opposite conclusion.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx is a genus of two known species of feathered theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx (gr. "cola emplumada") es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios terópodos caudiptéridos

facts.statement: Caudipteryx lived approximately 125 million years ago during the early Cretaceous period in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Asia

facts.statement: Caudipteryx fossils were discovered in 1997 in the Yixian Formation near Sihetun in Liaoning, northeast China.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Caudipteryx fueron descubiertos en la Formación Yixian del área de Sihetun en la provincia de Liaoning noreste de China en 1997

facts.statement: The type species Caudipteryx zoui was described in 1998, and Caudipteryx dongi was described in 2000.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx zoui la especie tipo, en 1998, y Caudipteryx dongi, en 2000

facts.statement: The two species of Caudipteryx reached lengths of up to one meter, heights of 0.7 meters, and weighed between 6 and 7 kilograms.
facts.quote: En general, las 2 especies de Caudipterix llegaban a medir hasta un metro de longitud y 0,7 de altura y a pesar entre 6 y 7 kilogramos

facts.statement: Caudipteryx possessed a strong beak, feathered tail and arms, a small skull, a lightweight skeleton, and long fingers with sharp claws.
facts.quote: Este celurosaurio poseía un pico fuerte, cola y brazos emplumados, cráneo pequeño, esqueleto ligero y largos dedos con garras filudas

facts.statement: The tail was short, constituting only one-quarter of the body length.
facts.quote: La cola era corta y constituía solo una cuarta parte de la longitud del cuerpo

facts.statement: The feathers are similar in outline to modern bird flight feathers, consisting of a feather banner made of a rachis with a vane of interlaced barbs and barbules.
facts.quote: Las plumas son similares en contorno a las plumas oscilantes de las aves modernas, consisten en una bandera de plumas hecha de un raquis con un vexilo de barbas y barbilas entrelazadas

facts.statement: The shortness and symmetry of the feathers, along with the short arms relative to body size, indicate that Caudipteryx could not fly.
facts.quote: Lo corto y la simetría de las plumas, junto con lo corto de los brazos con respecto al tamaño de cuerpo, indican que Caudipteryx no podía volar

facts.statement: The genus was named and identified by Philip Currie, Ji Qiang, Mark Norell, and Ji Shuan based on the holotype NGMC 97-4-A, a skeleton with feathers, and the paratype NGMC 97-9-A.
facts.quote: Este género fue nombrado e identificado por Philip Currie, Ji Qiang, Mark Norell y Ji Shuan basandoce en el holotipo NGMC 97-4-A, un esqueleto con plumas y el paratipo NGMC 97-9-A

facts.statement: The fossil was collected in the summer of 1998 by the team of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
facts.quote: El fósil fue recolectado en el verano boreal de 1998 por el equipo del Instituto de Paleontología de Vertebrados y Paleoantropología de la Academia de Ciencias China

facts.statement: It is debated whether Caudipteryx is a member of Oviraptorosauria, a bird, or both, and whether birds are or are not dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx es un miembro de Oviraptorosauria, o un ave, o ambos, y las aves pueden ser o no dinosaurios

facts.statement: Not all scientists support the theory that Caudipteryx is indisputably non-avian; some, like Alan Feduccia, doubt the consensus that birds are theropods and argue Caudipteryx is a non-flying bird unrelated to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, no todos los científicos apoyan la teoría que Caudipteryx es indiscutiblemente no aviano, y algunos dudan del consenso entre los paleontólogos como Alan Feduccia, que se opone que las aves son terópodos y Caudipteryx es un ave no voladora no relacionada con los dinosaurios

facts.statement: Jones et al. found in 2000 that Caudipteryx is a bird based on mathematical comparisons of body proportions between non-flying birds and non-avian theropods.
facts.quote: Jones et al. en 2000 encontraron que Caudipteryx es un ave debido a comparaciones matemáticas en las proporciones del cuerpo entre aves no voladores y terópodos no avianos

facts.statement: Most paleontologists who performed cladistic analysis agree that Caudipteryx is a basal member of the family Oviraptoridae and that oviraptorids are non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Es consenso entre la mayoría de los paleontólogos que realizaron el análisis cladístico, que Caudipteryx es un miembro basal de la familia Oviraptoridae, y los ovirráptoridos son dinosaurios no avianos

facts.statement: Halszka Osmolska et al. (2004) concluded in their cladistic analysis that Caudipteryx possesses more bird-like characteristics than current oviraptorids, placing the clade between birds and considering Caudipteryx to be both an oviraptorid and a bird.
facts.quote: Halszka Osmolska et al. (2004) han llegado a una conclusión distinta en su análisis cladístico. Ellos observaron que posee más características de aves que los ovirráptorido actualmente colocando al clado entre aves, es más considera a Caudipteryx es a la vez ovirráptorido y ave

facts.statement: Stephen Czerkas and Larry Martin concluded that Caudipteryx is not a theropod dinosaur, arguing that all maniraptorans are non-flying birds that evolved from non-dinosaurian archosaur ancestors.
facts.quote: Otros como Stephen Czerkas y Larry Martin concluyeron que Caudipteryx no es un dinosaurio téropodo. Ellos sostienen que Caudipteryx, como todos los manirraptores, son aves no voladoras, y que las aves evolucionaron de ancestros arcosaurios no dinosaurios

facts.statement: Lamanna et al. performed a cladistic analysis during the description of Anzu wyliei, placing Caudipteryx within Oviraptorosauria.
facts.quote: En la descripción de Anzu wyliei, miembro de la familia Caenagnathoidea, Lamanna et al. realizaron un análisis cladistico con su posterior cladograma colocando Caudipteryx dentro Oviraptorosauria

facts.statement: Caudipteryx is considered an omnivore.
facts.quote: Caudipteryx es considerado como un omnívoro.

facts.statement: Gastroliths have been preserved in at least two Caudipteryx specimens, NGMC 97 4 A and NGMC 97 9 A.
facts.quote: En al menos dos especímenes de Caudipteryx, NGMC 97 4 A y NGMC 97 9 A, se han preservados gastrolitos.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx had a bird-like beak covered with long upper teeth.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico semejante al de las aves revestido de dientes superiores largos.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx primarily fed on insects, small mammals, primitive birds, and lizards.
facts.quote: El caudipteryx se alimentaba principalmente de insectos, mamíferos pequeños, aves primitivas y lagartijas.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx was a runner and likely very fast, although its speed has not been formally calculated.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio era corredor y probablemente muy veloz, aunque no se ha calculado su velocidad de manera formal.

facts.statement: Researchers propose that Caudipteryx used its speed to escape large predators rather than to catch prey.
facts.quote: Se ha propuesto que el Caudipteryx no usaba su velocidad para atrapar presas sino para escapar de grandes depredadores.

facts.statement: Symmetrical pennaceous feathers with barbs and rachises measuring 15-20 centimeters long were held in Caudipteryx's hands.
facts.quote: En las manos de Caudipteryx sostenían plumas simétricas y penaceas que tenían barbas y raquis y que medían entre 15-20 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: No Caudipteryx zoui fossil preserves secondary feathers attached to the forearms, unlike dromaeosaurids, Archaeopteryx, and modern birds.
facts.quote: Ningún fósil de Caudipteryx zoui conserva plumas secundarias adheridas a los antebrazos, como se encuentra en dromeosáuridos, Archaeopteryx y aves modernas.

facts.statement: An additional fan of feathers existed on Caudipteryx's short tail.
facts.quote: Un abanico adicional de plumas existió en su cola corta.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx's tail was like a large feather fan reaching up to 2 decimeters, fanning out from short tail bones to act as stabilizers when running.
facts.quote: La cola del Caudipterix era como un gran abanico de plumas que llegaba a medir hasta 2 decímetros y se desplegaba desde los huesos cortos de su cola, actuando como estabilizadores cuando corría.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx's tail was very short compared to that of any other non-avian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Su cola era muy corta en comparación con la de cualquier otro dinosaurio no aviano.

facts.statement: The shape of the feathers and the overall body structure demonstrate that Caudipteryx was terrestrial rather than flying.
facts.quote: La forma de la pluma y la estructura total del cuerpo demuestran que el caudipterix no era volador sino terrestre.

facts.statement: Long feathers may have been brightly colored solely to be displayed to scare enemies or attract mates.
facts.quote: Las plumas largas pudieron ser de colores brillantes pero tan solo para desplegarlas, para asustar a los enemigos o para atraer a la pareja.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx's body was covered in silky, padded feathers, likely used to protect against the cold.
facts.quote: El cuerpo del Caudipterix estaba cubierto de plumas sedosas y acolchadas, usadas probablemente para protegerse del frío.

facts.statement: Caudipteryx belongs to the parent group Oviraptorosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Oviraptorosauria

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Caudipteryx is Caudipteryx zoui.
facts.quote: Type species: Caudipteryx zoui

facts.statement: Caudipteryx lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
